label: intro_main_thm
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{intro_main_thm}
Let $G$ be a connected reductive group over $k$, equipped with a Frobenius endomorphism $F$ on $G$ such that $G$ has property $\mathscr{D}$-orbit. Assume that $\ell$ and $p$ are good for $G$, and $\ell$ does not divide $p\,\lvert Z(G)^F/Z^0(G)^F\rvert$. Let $\Pi$ be a unipotent cuspidal $\mathbb{Q}_\ell^{\rm un}$-representation of $G^{F^\ell}$ such that $\Pi\simeq \Pi^\sigma$. Then, for any $\mathbb{Z}_\ell^{\rm un}[G^{F^\ell}\rtimes\langle\sigma\rangle]$-stable lattice $\mathcal{L}$ in $\Pi$, the Tate cohomology $\widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L})$ is irreducible as a representation of $G^F$. Moreover, the first Tate cohomology group $\widehat{\rm H}^1(\sigma,\mathcal{L})$ is trivial.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
\normalfont
An $R$-representation $(\pi,V)$ of $G^F$ is called {\it cuspidal} if $^*R_L^G(V)=0$ for all $F$-stable Levi subgroups $L$ of all proper $F$-stable parabolic subgroups $P$ of $G$.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
\normalfont
When $L=T$ an $F$-stable maximal torus in $G$ and $\theta$ is an one-dimensional character of $T^F$, then $R_T^G(\theta)$ is called a {\it Deligne--Lusztig character}.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
\normalfont
An irreducible $\ell$-adic representation $\pi$ of $G^F$ is said to be {\it unipotent} if there exists an $F$-stable maximal torus $T$ of $G$ such that $\pi$ occurs in $R_T^G(1)$, i.e.,
$$\langle \chi_\pi, R_{T}^G(1)\rangle_{G^F}\ne 0, $$ where $1$ is the trivial representation of $T^F$.
head: environment

title: Theorem
body_md: When $p$ is a good prime for $G$, then an irreducible $\ell$-adic representation $\rho$ of $G^F$ has a unique unipotent support.
head: environment

label: mod_l_irr_unip_cusp
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{mod_l_irr_unip_cusp}
Let $G$ be a connected reductive group over $k$, equipped with a Frobenius morphism $F:G\rightarrow G$. Assume that the primes $\ell$ and $p$ are good for $G$, and $\ell$ does not divide $p\,\lvert Z(G)^F/Z^0(G)^F\rvert$. Then, the mod-$\ell$ reduction of any unipotent cuspidal $\ell$-adic representation of $G^F$ is irreducible.

The induced representation $\Gamma_u^{G^F}:= {\rm Ind}_{U_{1.5}^F}^{G^F}(\widetilde{\psi}_u)$ is called the {\it generalized Gelfand--Graev representation} of $\textbf{G}^F$ associated with $u$.

label: TV_isom
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{TV_isom}
Let $H$ be a finite group, and $\sigma$ be an automorphism of $H$ of prime order $\ell$. Let $K$ be a $\sigma$-stable subgroup of $H$. Then, for any $\Lambda[K\rtimes \sigma]$-module $V$, the restriction map 
$$ \big({\rm Ind}_K^H(v)\big)^\sigma \rightarrow {\rm Ind}_{K^\sigma}^{H^\sigma}(\widehat{\rm H}^i(\sigma, V)) $$
$$ \varphi\mapsto \varphi|_{H^\sigma} $$
induces an isomorphism of $H^\sigma$-representations
$$ \widehat{\rm H}^i\big(\sigma, {\rm ind}_K^H(V)\big) \simeq 
{\rm Ind}_{K^\sigma}^{H^\sigma}(\widehat{\rm H}^i(\sigma,V)). $$
head: environment

label: Tate_cuspidal
title: Proposition
body_md:
\cite[Corollary 3.3.3]{dhar2025jacquet}\label{Tate_cuspidal}
Let $G$ be a connected reductive algebraic group with the Frobenius map $F$. Let $\tau$ be a cuspidal $\ell$-adic representation of $G^{F^\ell}$ such that $\tau$ extends as a representation of $G^{F^\ell}\rtimes\sigma$. Then, for any $\Lambda[G^{F^\ell}\rtimes\sigma]$-stable lattice $\mathcal{L}$ in $\tau$, the Tate cohomology groups $\widehat{\rm H}^i(\sigma,\mathcal{L})$ are cuspidal.
head: environment

label: char_iden
title: Lemma
body_md:
\cite[Lemma 5.2.1]{dhar2025jacquet}\label{char_iden}
Let $J$ be a cyclic group of prime order $\ell$, and let $G$ be a finite group with an action of $J$. Let $M$ be a 
$\Lambda[G\rtimes J]$-module such that $M$ is a free $\Lambda$-module of 
finite rank. Assume that $\widehat{{\rm H}}^1(J, M) =0$. Then
$$ {\rm Tr}(g|_{\widehat{{\rm H}}^0(J, M)})=\overline{{\rm Tr}(g|_M)}, $$ 
for all $g\in G^J$.
head: environment

label: Tate_GGGR
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{Tate_GGGR}
Let $u\in G^F$ be a unipotent element. Then we have the $G^F$-isomorphisms
$$ \widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma, \Gamma_u^{G^{F^\ell}}) \simeq \big(\overline{\Gamma}_u^{G^F}\big)^{(\ell)}. $$
Moreover, the first Tate cohomology group $\widehat{\rm H}^1(\sigma,\Gamma_u^{G^{F^\ell}})$ is trivial.
head: environment

label: Tate_isom_2
title: Proof
body_md:
Since $U_{1.5}^{F^\ell}$ is a $\sigma$-stable subgroup of $G^{F^\ell}$, we have the following exact sequence of non-abelian cohomology sets:
$$ 1\longrightarrow U_{1.5}^F\longrightarrow G^F\longrightarrow \big(U_{1.5}^{F^\ell}\backslash G^{F^\ell}\big)^\sigma\longrightarrow {\rm H}^1(\sigma,U_{1.5}^{F^\ell}). $$
Since $U_{1.5}^{F^\ell}$ is a finite $p$-group and $\ell\ne p$, the cohomology set ${\rm H}^1(\sigma,U_{1.5}^{F^\ell})$ is trivial. From the preceding exact sequence, we get the equality of sets
$$ \big(U_{1.5}^{F^\ell}\backslash G^{F^\ell}\big)^\sigma = U_{1.5}^F\backslash G^F. $$
Using Theorem \ref{TV_isom}, we get the following isomorphism of $G^F$-representations
\begin{equation}\label{Tate_isom_2}
\widehat{\rm H}^i(\sigma,\Gamma_u^{G^{F^\ell}})\simeq {\rm Ind}_{U_{1.5}^F}^{G^F}(\widehat{\rm H}^i(\sigma, \widetilde{\eta}_u)).
\end{equation}
For $x\in U_{1.5}^F$, we see that $F(\lambda(f_{\rm spr}(x)))=\lambda(f_{\rm spr}(x))$, i.e., $\lambda(f_{\rm spr}(x))\in\mathbb{F}_q$. Hence, $\widetilde{\eta}_u(x)=(\widetilde{\psi}_u(x))^\ell$. Thus, we get that $\widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\widetilde{\eta}_u) \simeq \overline{\widetilde{\psi}_u}^{\ell}$, where $\overline{\widetilde{\psi}_u}$ is the mod-$\ell$ reduction of $\widetilde{\psi}_u$. Also note that $\widehat{\rm H}^1(\sigma,\widetilde{\eta}_u)
|_{U_{2}^F}=\widehat{\rm H}^1(\sigma,\widetilde{\eta}_u|
_{U_{2}^{F^\ell}})=\widehat{\rm H}^1(\sigma,\eta_u) = 0$. Then it follows from the isomorphism (\ref{Tate_isom_2}) that $\widehat{\rm H}^1(\sigma,\Gamma_u^{G^{F^\ell}})$ is trivial, and 
$$ \widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\Gamma_u^{G^{F^\ell}}) \simeq (\overline{\Gamma}_u^{G^F})^{(\ell)} $$
as $G^F$-representations. Hence, the lemma follows.
head: environment

label: Tate_injection
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{Tate_injection}
Let $u$ be a unipotent element in $G^F$. Then, for any $[G^{F^\ell}\rtimes\sigma]$-module $\mathcal{L}$, the natural map 
$$ \widehat{\rm H}^i(\sigma,\mathcal{L})_{{U_{1.5}^{F},
\overline{\widetilde{\psi}}_u}}\longrightarrow \widehat{\rm H}^i(\sigma,\mathcal{L}_{U_{1.5}^{F^\ell},\widetilde{\eta}_u}) $$ 
is an injection for each $i\in\{0,1\}$, where $\overline{\widetilde{\psi}}_u$ is the mod-$\ell$ reduction of $\widetilde{\psi}_u$.
head: environment

label: lift_sum_1
title: Proof
body_md:
The proof follows a similar line of arguments as in \cite[Theorem 3.3.2]{dhar2025jacquet}. For the notational convenience, we put $U_\ell=U_{1.5}^{F^\ell}$ and $U=U_{1.5}^F$. For $i\in\{0,1\}$, let $\varphi_i$ be the natural map
$$ \widehat{{\rm H}}^i(\sigma, \mathcal{L}(U_\ell,
\widetilde{\eta}_u))\rightarrow \widehat{{\rm H}}^i(\sigma, \mathcal{L}). $$ 
\vspace{0.1 cm}
\textbf{Claim.} The image of $\varphi_i$ is $\widehat{\rm H}^i(\sigma,\mathcal{L})(U,\overline{\widetilde{\psi}}_u)$.
\vspace{0.1 cm}\\
We consider the case $i=0$. Let $v$ be in the image of $\varphi_0$, and
let $\tilde{v}$ be a lift of $v$ in $\mathcal{L}(U_\ell,\widetilde{\eta}_u)^\sigma$.
Then we have
\begin{equation}\label{lift_sum_1}
\sum_{x\in U_\ell}\widetilde{\eta}_u^{-1}(x)\Pi(x)\tilde{v} = 0.
\end{equation}
Since $\sigma$ acts freely on $U_\ell\setminus U$, there exists a subset $\mathcal{U}\subseteq U_\ell\setminus U$ such that $U_\ell\setminus U$ is the disjoint union of $\sigma^i\mathcal{U}$ for $1\leq i\leq \ell$. Then, using the fact that $\tilde{v}$ is a $\sigma$-fixed vector, it follows from the identity (\ref{lift_sum_1}) that
\begin{align*}
\sum_{x\in U_\ell}\widetilde{\eta}_u^{-1}(x)\Pi(x) v 
&=\sum_{y\in U}\widetilde{\psi}_u^{-1}(y)\Pi(y) v + \sum_{x\in U_\ell\setminus U} \widetilde{\eta}_u^{-1}(x)\Pi(x)v\\
&=\sum_{y\in U}\widetilde{\psi}_u^{-1}(y)\Pi(y) v + \sum_{i=1}^\ell\sum_{z\in\mathcal{U}}\widetilde{\psi}_u^{-1}(\sigma^i(z))\Pi(\sigma^i(z))\tilde{v}\\
&=\sum_{y\in U}\widetilde{\psi}_u^{-1}(y)\Pi(y) v
+ {\rm Nr}\big(\sum_{z\in\mathcal{U}}\widetilde{\eta}_u^{-1}(z)\Pi(z)\tilde{v}\big).
\end{align*}
Since
$$ {\rm Nr}\big(\sum_{z\in\mathcal{U}}\widetilde{\eta}_u^{-1}(z)\Pi(z)\tilde{v}\big) = 0 $$ 
in $\widehat{{\rm H}}^0(\mathcal{L})$, it follows from the above identity that
$$ \sum_{y\in U} 
\overline{\widetilde{\psi}}_u^{-1}(y)\,\Pi(y)v = 0. $$ 
This implies that the vector $v$
belongs to
$\widehat{{\rm H}}^0(\mathcal{L})(U,\overline{\widetilde{\psi}}_u)$.
Conversely, let $w$ be an element of
$\widehat{{\rm H}}^0(\mathcal{L})(U,\overline{\widetilde{\psi}}_u)$.
Let $\tilde{w}$ be a lift of
$w$ in $\mathcal{L}^\sigma$. Consider the element
$$ \tilde{w}_1 = \tilde{w} - \lvert U_\ell\rvert \sum_{x\in U_\ell}
\widetilde{\eta}_u^{-1}(x)\Pi(x)\tilde{w}. $$
Then $\tilde{w}_1$ belongs to $\mathcal{L}(U_\ell,\widetilde{\eta}_u)^\sigma$ 
and $\varphi_0(\tilde{w}_1) = w$. 
                  
                               
                                                   
                                            
                                           
Thus, we prove the claim for
$i=0$. The case $i=1$ is similar. Now, we consider the following short exact sequence of $\Lambda[\sigma]$-modules
$$ 0\longrightarrow \mathcal{L}(U_\ell,\widetilde{\eta}_u)\longrightarrow \mathcal{L}\longrightarrow \mathcal{L}_{U_\ell,\widetilde{\eta}_u}\longrightarrow 0. $$
The corresponding long exact sequence of Tate cohomology groups gives the following exact sequences:
$$ \widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L}(U_\ell,\widetilde{\eta}_u))\xrightarrow {\varphi_0} \widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L})\longrightarrow \widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L}_{U_\ell,
\widetilde{\eta}_u}) $$
and 
$$ \widehat{\rm H}^1(\sigma,\mathcal{L}(U_\ell,\widetilde{\eta}_u))\xrightarrow {\varphi_1} \widehat{\rm H}^1(\sigma,\mathcal{L})\longrightarrow \widehat{\rm H}^1(\sigma,\mathcal{L}_{U_\ell,
\widetilde{\eta}_u}). $$
Since the image of $\varphi_i$ is $\widehat{\rm H}^i(\sigma,\mathcal{L})(U,\overline{\widetilde{\psi}}_u)$, the natural map 
$$ \widehat{\rm H}^i(\sigma,\mathcal{L})_{U,\overline{\widetilde{\psi}}_u}\rightarrow \widehat{\rm H}^i(\sigma,\mathcal{L}_{U_\ell,
\widetilde{\eta}_u}) $$
is injective. Hence, the lemma follows.
head: environment

label: sigma_stable_mult_1_gggr
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: sigma_stable_mult_1
title: Proof
body_md:
Consider the unipotent class $\sigma(C)$ of $G^{F^\ell}$. Since $C$ is the unipotent support of $\Pi$, the unipotent class $\sigma(C)$ is the unipotent support of $\Pi^\sigma$. Since $\Pi\simeq \Pi^\sigma$, we get that $\sigma(C)$ is also a unipotent support of $\Pi$. By uniqueness of $C$, we have
$\sigma(C) =C$, i.e., $C$ is $\sigma$-stable. From (\ref{mult_1_gggr}), we get the following identity
\begin{equation}\label{sigma_stable_mult_1}
\sum_{[u]\in C^{F^\ell}/G^{F^\ell}}\langle\gamma_u^{G^{F^\ell}},\chi_\Pi\rangle = 1.
\end{equation}
Let $[u]\in C^{F^\ell}/G^{F^\ell}$. Suppose $[u]$ is not $\sigma$-stable and $\langle\gamma_u^{G^{F^\ell}},\chi_\Pi\rangle=1$, then using the fact that $\chi_\Pi=\chi_\Pi^\sigma$, we get $\langle\gamma_{\sigma(u)}^{G^{F^\ell}},\chi_\Pi\rangle=1$, which contradicts to the identity (\ref{sigma_stable_mult_1}). Hence, there exists exactly one $\sigma$-stable orbit $[u]$ in $C^{F^\ell}/G^{F^\ell}$ such that
$$ \langle\gamma_u^{G^{F^\ell}},\chi_\Pi\rangle = 1. $$
Thus, we get the required lemma.
head: environment

label: sigma_action_uni_cusp
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{sigma_action_uni_cusp}
Let $\Pi$ be a unipotent cuspidal $\ell$-adic representation of $G^{F^\ell}$ such that $\Pi\simeq \Pi^\sigma$. Then $\Pi$ extends uniquely as a representation of $G^{F^\ell}\rtimes \sigma$.
head: environment

title: Proof
head: environment

label: classical_descent
title: Remark
body_md:
\normalfont\label{classical_descent}
Many classical algebraic groups $G$ admit the property $\mathscr{D}$-orbit; a list is given below.
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{|c c|} 
 \hline 
 $G$ & $G^F$ \\ 
 \hline\hline
 ${\rm GL}_n$ & ${\rm GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ \\ 
 \hline
 ${\rm GL}_n$ & ${\rm U}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ \\
 \hline
 ${\rm Sp}_{2n}$ & ${\rm Sp}_{2n}(\mathbb{F}_q)$ \\
 \hline
 ${\rm SO}_{2n+1}$ & ${\rm SO}_{2n+1}(\mathbb{F}_q)$ \\
 \hline
 ${\rm SO}_{2n}$ & ${\rm SO}_{2n}(\mathbb{F}_q)$ \\ 
 \hline
 ${\rm Spin}_{n}, n\geq 5$ & ${\rm Spin}_{n}(\mathbb{F}_q)$ \\
 \hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Let $G$ be one of the classical algebraic groups listed above. For any unipotent $u\in G^{F^\ell}$, the component group $\pi_0(C_G(u))=C_G(u)/C_G(u)^0$ is an abelian $2$-group. Since $\ell$ is an odd prime, $\ell$ does not divide $\lvert \pi_0(C_G(u))\rvert$. Hence, $\sigma$ acts trivially on $\pi_0(C_G(u))$, and we get the required bijection.
head: environment

label: first_tate_trivial
title: Theorem
head: environment

label: first_tate_equ_1
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a $\Lambda[G^{F^\ell}\rtimes\sigma]$-stable lattice in $\Pi$. Since the Tate cohomology group $\widehat{\rm H}^1(\sigma,\mathcal{L})$ is cuspidal (by Proposition \ref{Tate_cuspidal}), it follows from the Frobenius reciprocity that
\begin{equation}\label{first_tate_equ_1}
{\rm Hom}_{G^F}\big(R_L^G(\overline{\Gamma}_C^{L^F}),
\widehat{\rm H}^1(\sigma,\mathcal{L})\big) = 0,
\end{equation}
for all proper $1$-split Levi subgroups $L$ of $G$ and for all $F$-stable unipotent classes $C$ of $L$ which are cuspidal for $L_{\rm ad}$. 

Let $C_\Pi$ be the unipotent support of $\Pi$. It follows from \cite[Proposition 3.1]{Dudas_Malle_irr_mod_l} that 
$$ {\rm dim}_{\mathcal{K}}\,{\rm Hom}_{G^{F^\ell}}(\Gamma_{C_\Pi}^{G^{F^\ell}}\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal{K},\Pi) =1 $$
or equivalently,
$$ \sum_{[w]\in C_\Pi^{F^\ell}/G^{F^\ell}}{\rm dim}_{\mathcal{K}}\,{\rm Hom}_{G^{F^\ell}}(\Gamma_{C_\Pi}^{G^{F^\ell}}
\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal{K},\Pi) =1, $$
where $C_{\Pi}^{F^\ell}/G^{F^\ell}$ is the set of distinct $G^{F^\ell}$-orbits in $C_\Pi^{F^\ell}$. Note that $C_\Pi$ is $F$-stable. By Lemma \ref{sigma_stable_mult_1_gggr}, there exists a $\sigma$-stable orbit $[w]\in C^{F^\ell}/G^{F^\ell}$ such that
                                                                                                                 
                                                           
$$ {\rm dim}_{\mathcal{K}}\,{\rm Hom}_{G^F}(\Gamma_w^{G^{F^\ell}}\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal{K}, \Pi) = 1,$$
and we have
$$ {\rm dim}_{\mathcal{K}}\,{\rm Hom}_{G^F}(\Gamma_{w'}^{G^{F^\ell}}\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal{K}, \Pi) = 0, $$
for all $\sigma$-stable orbits $[w']\in C^{F^\ell}/G^{F^\ell}$ with $[w']\ne [w]$. Since $G$ has the property $\mathscr{D}$-orbit, there exist $u, u'\in G^F$ with $[u]\ne [u']$ in $C_\Pi^F/G^F$ such that $[u]=[w]$ and $[u']=[w']$ in $C_\Pi^{F^\ell}/G^{F^\ell}$. Now, using Frobenius reciprocity, we get
$$ {\rm dim}_{\mathcal{K}}(\Pi_{U_{1.5}^{F^\ell},\widetilde{\eta}_u}) = 1,\,\,\,\,\,\, {\rm dim}_{\mathcal{K}}(\Pi_{U_{1.5}'^{F^\ell},\widetilde{\eta}_{u'}}) = 0, $$
where $U_{1.5}'$ is the $F$-stable subgroup of $G$ associated with the unipotent element $u'$. Thus, the space of coinvariants $\mathcal{L}_{U_{1.5}^{F^\ell},
\widetilde{\eta}_u}$ is a free $\Lambda$-module of rank one, and $\mathcal{L}_{U_{1.5}'^{F^\ell},
\widetilde{\eta}_{u'}} = 0$ for $[u']\ne [u]$ in $C_\Pi^{F}/G^{F}$. Hence, 
$$ \widehat{\rm H}^1(\sigma,\mathcal{L}_{U_{1.5}^{F^\ell},
\widetilde{\eta}_u}) = 0,\,\,\,\,\,\, \widehat{\rm H}^1(\sigma,\mathcal{L}_{U_{1.5}'^{F^\ell},
\widetilde{\eta}_{u'}})=0. $$
Using Lemma \ref{Tate_injection}, we get that 
$\widehat{\rm H}^1(\sigma,\mathcal{L})_{U_{1.5}^F,\overline{\widetilde{\psi}}_u}$ is trivial for all $u\in C_\Pi^F$--which is equivalent to saying
\begin{equation}\label{first_Tate_equ_2}
{\rm Hom}_{G^F}(\overline{\Gamma}_{C_\Pi}^{G^F},\widehat{\rm H}^1(\sigma,\mathcal{L})) = \{0\}.
\end{equation}
For an $F$-stable unipotent class $D$ in $G$ such that $D\ne C_\Pi$, we have 
$$ {\rm dim}_{\mathcal{K}}\,{\rm Hom}_{G^{F^\ell}}(\Gamma_D^{G^{F^\ell}}\otimes_\Lambda
\mathcal{K},\Pi) =0. $$
Using a similar line arguments as in the case of $C_\Pi$, we get that $\widehat{\rm H}^1(\sigma,\mathcal{L})_{U_{1.5}^F,\overline{\widetilde{\psi}}_u}$ is trivial for all $u\in D^F$, and hence
\begin{equation}\label{first_Tate_equ_3}
{\rm Hom}_{G^F}(\overline{\Gamma}_D^{G^F},\widehat{\rm H}^1(\sigma,\mathcal{L})) = \{0\}.
\end{equation}
From (\ref{first_tate_equ_1}), (\ref{first_Tate_equ_2}) and (\ref{first_Tate_equ_3}), we obtain 
$$ {\rm Hom}_{G^F}(\mathscr{P}, \widehat{\rm H}^1(\sigma,\mathcal{L})) = \{0\}. $$
Since $\mathscr{P}$ is a progenerator, the functor ${\rm Hom}_{G^F}(\mathscr{P},\_)$ is faithful. Hence, the space $\widehat{\rm H}^1(\sigma,\mathcal{L})$ is trivial.
head: environment

label: Pro_gen_1
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: equ_5
title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\Pi$ is cuspidal, the Tate cohomology group $\widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L})$ is also cuspidal by Proposition \ref{Tate_cuspidal}. Therefore, for any proper $1$-split Levi subgroup $L$ of $G$, we have $^\ast R_L^G(\widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L}))=0$. Frobenius reciprocity gives
\begin{equation}\label{equ_5}
{\rm Hom}_{G^F}(R_L^G(\overline{\Gamma}_{C}^{L^F}),\widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L})) \simeq 
{\rm Hom}_{L^F}\big(\overline{\Gamma}_{C}^{L^F},\,^\ast R_L^G(\widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L}))\big) = \{0\},
\end{equation}
for all $F$-stable unipotent classes $C$ in $L$ that are cuspidal for $L_{\rm ad}$. Let $C_\Pi$ be the unipotent support of $\Pi$. Since $\Pi\simeq \Pi^\sigma$, uniqueness of $C_\Pi$ shows that $C_\Pi$ is $F$-stable. Note that 
$$ {\rm dim}_{\mathcal{K}}\,{\rm Hom}_{G^{F^\ell}}(\Gamma_{C_\Pi}^{G^{F^\ell}}\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal{K},\Pi) = 1. $$
By applying Lemma \ref{sigma_stable_mult_1_gggr} and the $\mathscr{D}$-orbit property of $G$, there exists a unipotent class $[u]$ in $C_\Pi^{F^\ell}/G^{F^\ell}$ with $\sigma(u)=u$ such that
$$ {\rm dim}_{\mathcal{K}}\,{\rm Hom}_{G^{F^\ell}}(\Gamma_u^{G^{F^\ell}}\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal{K},\Pi) = 1 $$
and 
$$ {\rm dim}_{\mathcal{K}}\,{\rm Hom}_{G^{F^\ell}}(\Gamma_{u'}^{G^{F^\ell}}\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal{K},\Pi) = 0 $$
for all $[u']\in (C_\Pi^{F^\ell}/G^{F^\ell})^\sigma$ with $\sigma(u')=u'$ and $[u]\ne [u']$. The above two identities shows that $\mathcal{L}_{U_{1.5}^{F^\ell},\widetilde{\eta}_u}$ is a free $\Lambda$-module of rank one, and $\mathcal{L}_{U_{1.5}'^{F^\ell},\widetilde{\eta}_{u'}}$ is trivial. Since $\sigma$ acts trivially on these modules, using (\ref{Tate_coinv_free}) and Lemma \ref{Tate_injection}, we get that
$$ {\rm dim}_{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_\ell} \widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L})_{U_{1.5}^F,\overline{\widetilde{\psi}}_u} \leq 1, $$
for all $[u]$ in $C_\Pi^F/G^F$. Since $U_{1.5}^F$ is a $p$-group and $\ell\ne p$, we have ${\rm Hom}_{U_{1.5}^F}(\widetilde{\psi}_u,\widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L}))\simeq \widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L})_{U_{1.5}^F,\widetilde{\psi}_u}$. Then it follows from Frobenius reciprocity that
\begin{equation}\label{equ_1}
{\rm dim}_{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_\ell}\,{\rm Hom}_{G^F}(\overline{\Gamma}_{C_\Pi}^{G^F}, \widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L}))\leq 1.
\end{equation}
Let $C'\ne C_\Pi$ be an $F$-stable cuspidal unipotent class in $G$. Since 
$$ {\rm dim}_{\mathcal{K}}\,{\rm Hom}_{G^{F^\ell}}(\Gamma_{C'}^{G^{F^\ell}}\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal{K},\Pi) = 0, $$
it follows from a similar argument as in the case of $C_\Pi$ that 
\begin{equation}\label{equ_2}
{\rm dim}_{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_\ell}\, {\rm Hom}_{G^{F}}(\overline{\Gamma}_{C'}^{G^F}, \widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L})) = 0.
\end{equation}
Then it follows from (\ref{equ_5}), (\ref{equ_1}) and (\ref{equ_2}) that
$$ {\rm dim}_{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_\ell}\, {\rm Hom}_{G^F}(\mathscr{P},\widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L}))\leq 1. $$
Hence, we get the required lemma.
head: environment

label: Tate_irr
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{Tate_irr}
Let $G$ be a connected reductive group with a Frobenius morphism $F$ on $G$ such that $G$ is simple of adjoint type. Assume that $G$ has the property $\mathscr{D}$-orbit and that $p$ is good for $G$. Let $\Pi$ be a cuspidal unipotent $\ell$-adic representation of $G^{F^\ell}$ such that $\Pi^\sigma\simeq \Pi$. Then, for any $\Lambda[G^{F^\ell}\rtimes\sigma]$-stable lattice $\mathcal{L}$ in $\Pi$, the Tate cohomology group $\widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L})$ is irreducible as a representation of $G^F$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider the the composition series of $\widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L})$:
$$ 0=\xi_0\subseteq \xi_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq \xi_r=\widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L}). $$
By the exactness of the functor ${\rm Hom}_{G^F}(\mathscr{P},\_)$, we have
$$ {\rm dim}_{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_\ell}\,{\rm Hom}_{G^F}(\mathscr{P},\widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L})) = \sum_{i=1}^r {\rm dim}_{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_\ell}\,{\rm Hom}_{G^F}(\mathscr{P},\xi_i/\xi_{i-1}). $$
Since each $\xi_i/\xi_{i-1}$ is irreducible, the space ${\rm Hom}_{G^F}(\mathscr{P},\xi_i/\xi_{i-1})$ is non-trivial. Hence, 
$$ {\rm dim}_{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_\ell}\,{\rm Hom}_{G^F}(\mathscr{P},\xi_i/\xi_{i-1})\geq 1, $$
for each $i$.
Since ${\rm dim}_{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_\ell}\, {\rm Hom}_{G^F}(\mathscr{P},\widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L})) = 1$ (by Lemma \ref{Pro_gen_1}), it follows from the above identity that $r\leq 1$. Note that $\widehat{\rm H}^1(\sigma,\mathcal{L})$ is trivial (by Theorem \ref{first_tate_trivial}). Then, applying Lemma \ref{char_iden}, we get the following relation
$$ {\rm Tr}(g|_{\widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L})}) = \overline{\chi_\Pi(g)} $$
for all $g\in G^F$. Since the mod-$\ell$ reduction $r_\ell(\Pi)$ is irreducible (see Theorem \ref{mod_l_irr_unip_cusp}), its trace is non-zero, and it follows from the above trace identity that $\widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L})$ is non-trivial. This implies that $r=1$, and hence proving the $G^F$-irreducibility of $\widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L})$.
head: environment

label: Tate_irr_general
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{Tate_irr_general}
Let $G$ be a connected reductive group with a Frobenius map $F$ defining an $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational structure on $G$ such that $G$ has property $\mathscr{D}$-orbit. Assume that $\ell$ and $p$ are good for $G$, and $\ell$ does not divide $p\,\lvert Z(G)^F/Z^0(G)^F\rvert$. Let $\Pi$ be a unipotent cuspidal $\ell$-adic representation of $G^{F^\ell}$ such that $\Pi\simeq \Pi^\sigma$. Then, for any $\Lambda[G^{F^\ell}\rtimes\sigma]$-stable lattice $\mathcal{L}$ in $\Pi$, the Tate cohomology group $\widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L})$ is irreducible. Moreover, the first Tate cohomology group $\widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L})$ is trivial.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If we fix a regular embedding $G\hookrightarrow \widetilde{G}$ with the center $Z(\widetilde{G})$ being connected, then the restriction of unipotent representations of $\widetilde{G}^F$ to $G^F$ remains irreducible (\cite[Proposition 17.4]{Geck_basic_set_unip_blocks}). Furthermore, the assumption on $\ell$ shows that the unipotent parts of the decomposition matrices of $G^F$ and $\widetilde{G}^F$ are equal (see \cite{Cabanes_Enguehard}). Therefore, without loss of generality, we can assume that $Z(G)$ is connected.

Since $Z(G)^F = Z(G^F)$ and the unipotent characters of $G^F$ are trivial on the center, we are further reduced to the case where $G$ is semisimple of adjoint type. Then $G$ is a direct product
$$ G = G_1^{n_1}\times\cdots\times G_r^{n_r}, $$
where each $G_i$ is simple of adjoint type and $F$ cyclically permutes the copies of $G_i$ in $G_i^{n_i}$, i.e., $F(g_1,\cdots,g_{n_i}) = (F(g_{n_i}), F(g_{n_i-1}),\dots,F(g_1))$. For one such block, projection onto the first component gives a group isomorphism $(G_i^{n_i})^F\simeq G_i^{F^{n_i}}$.
This isomorphism carries unipotent representations to unipotent representations. The finite group $G^F$ is a direct product
$$ G^F = G_1^{F^{n_1}}\times\cdots\times G_r^{F^{n_r}}. $$
Since $\Pi$ is a unipotent cuspidal $\ell$-adic representation of $G^{F^\ell}$, we have
$$ \Pi = \Pi_1\times\cdots\times \Pi_r, $$
where each $\Pi_i$ is a unipotent cuspidal $\ell$-adic representation of $G_i^{F^{\ell n_i}}$ such that $\Pi_i\simeq \Pi_i^\sigma$. Since each $G_i$ simple of adjoint type, there exists a unique action of $\sigma$ on $\Pi_i$ (see Lemma \ref{sigma_action_uni_cusp}), and hence we get a unique $\sigma$-action on $\Pi$. Choose a $\Lambda[G_i^{F^{\ell n_i}}\rtimes\sigma]$-stable lattice $\mathcal{L}_i$ in $\Pi_i$, and we set 
$$ \mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_1\otimes
\cdots\otimes\mathcal{L}_r. $$
Then $\mathcal{L}$ is a $\Lambda[G^{F^\ell}\rtimes\sigma]$-stable lattice in $\Pi$. Since each $\widehat{\rm H}^1(\sigma,\mathcal{L}_i)$ is trivial by Theorem \ref{first_tate_trivial}, it follows from \cite[Corollary 2.2]{Modular_moonshine_3} that the first Tate cohomology group $\widehat{\rm H}^1(\sigma,\mathcal{L})$ is trivial, and 
$$ \widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L}) = \widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L}_1)\otimes
\cdots\otimes\widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L}_r). $$
By Theorem \ref{Tate_irr}, each $\widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L}_i)$ is irreducible. Hence, $\widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L})$ is irreducible. Now, let us consider the short exact sequence of $\Lambda[\sigma]$-modules:
$$ 0\longrightarrow \mathcal{L}\xrightarrow{{\rm mult.} \ell}\mathcal{L}\longrightarrow\mathcal{L}\otimes_\Lambda\overline{\mathbb{F}}_\ell\longrightarrow 0. $$
The corresponding long exact sequence of Tate cohomology gives the following isomorphism
$$ \widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L})\simeq \widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L}\otimes_
\Lambda\overline{\mathbb{F}}_\ell). $$
Since the mod-$\ell$ reduction of $\Pi$ is irreducible (\cite[Theorem 3.2]{Dudas_Malle_irr_mod_l}), the Tate cohomology $\widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L}\otimes_\Lambda\overline{\mathbb{F}}_\ell)$ is independent of the choice of $\mathcal{L}$ (see \cite[Proposition 6.1]{TV_functoriality}). Thus, we get the irreducibility of $\widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L})$ for any $\Lambda[G^{F^\ell}\rtimes\sigma]$-stable lattice $\mathcal{L}$ in $\Pi$. This completes the proof.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
\normalfont
Let $G$, $\ell$, $p$ be as in Theorem \ref{Tate_irr_general}. Let $\Pi$ is a unipotent cuspidal $\ell$-adic representation of $G^{F^\ell}$ such that $\Pi\simeq \Pi^\sigma$. Recall that the mod-$\ell$ reduction $r_\ell(\Pi)$ is irreducible and is $\sigma$-stable. Then it follows from the proof of Theorem \ref{Tate_irr_general} that the Tate cohomology group $\widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,r_\ell(\Pi))$ is irreducible.
